thread:
maria: Heads up — we're seeing a new pattern in us-west1: long-lived gRPC streaming requests getting stuck in the edge and never finishing. Clients hang, backend shows no backlog. Memory on the edge-proxy worker climbs steadily during the run.

tony: Oof. Is this reproducible with our loadtest? any logs?

maria: Yep repro with streaming-infer load test (concurrency=40, stream-chunk-interval=100ms). After ~12m ~0.3% of streams go into a 'stalled' state. Edge worker RSS increases ~40–60MB/min while stalled. Attached small log excerpt below.

maria: ```
[2024-11-18T18:12:02Z] grpc: stream ID=534 open, no data seen for 34s
[2024-11-18T18:12:36Z] edge-proxy: http2: stream 534 half-closed (remote) but window_update not handled
[2024-11-18T18:13:05Z] runtime: goroutine blocked reading from upstream, conn stays ESTABLISHED
[2024-11-18T18:14:00Z] edge-proxy: worker heap growing; manual GC reclaimed small amount
```

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-20241118-334 (priority=P2) — tagging oncall.

infra-oncall: Looking. Quick checks: conntrack usage on edge hosts? NAT ephemeral ports?

kevin: I ran `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` and saw ~42k entries on one host (conntrack max 64k). Not full, but skewed to ESTABLISHED for outbound 10.0.0.0/16->0.0.0.0:*.

anya: Could be half-close semantics mismatch between upstream gRPC stack and our edge proxy (we use h2c passthrough + http2->tcp bridging). If the proxy buffers DATA until stream close, that could explain memory growth. Have we changed any http2 settings recently?

maria: We rolled `http2: enable_push=false` + bumped `max_concurrent_streams` last week for perf. No obvious changes to idle timeouts.

tony: Two hypotheses: 1) proxy isn't flushing window_update due to a bug when stream gets half-closed from client; 2) NAT/egress port reuse causes upstream TCP to be silently dropped and proxy keeps stream open waiting for reset. Logs point to window_update path.

kevin: I can capture tcpdump on a repro host next run, filter for stream IDs and look for RST/FIN.

anya: Also check the proxy's http2 flow-control stats (`/metrics` -> http2_server_flow_control_wait_count etc). Past issue showed `window_update_clamp` when many concurrent streams.

maria: Metric snippets from the affected host: `http2_server_window_update_pending_total=1234`, `http2_streams_half_closed_remote=12` during peak.

tony: Ok. Immediate mitigations: 1) increase `stream_idle_timeout` on the edge proxy from 30s -> 120s so half-closed streams are cleaned if nothing else; 2) enable aggressive window updates (lower threshold) to avoid head-of-line; 3) add conntrack/iptables rule to drop stale ESTABLISHED after shorter timeout on test pool. We need a canary roll.

infra-oncall: I prefer to avoid reducing conntrack TTL on prod until we confirm. Suggest canary in us-west1a only.

maria: I'll prepare a canary config: `stream_idle_timeout: 120s`, `http2_initial_window_size: 65535`, `http2_window_update_threshold: 0.25` (pseudo-config, envoy var names differ).

kevin: While canary runs I'll capture pcap and run `grpcurl -d @ -proto svc.proto` style streaming to replicate exactly.

anya: If window_update stats drop and memory stops climbing, we'll know it's flow-control. If not, look at half-close handing between our write loop and grpc-go's `CloseSend`.

tony: Also add a temporary logging change to dump per-stream state when stream age > 90s and bytes_sent unchanged. Keep it on for 1h.

infra-oncall: Rolling canary in us-west1a now (2 hosts). Patch pushed to canary group, config flip in 1m.

sre-bot: Deploy started: deploy/edge-proxy-config/20241118-332 -> canary (2 hosts).

maria: Can confirm canary has `stream_idle_timeout=120s`. I'll kick off the loadtest against canary pool.

kevin: pcap running. Also grabbed `netstat -anp | grep edge-proxy | wc -l` before/after.

maria: After 8m of load against canary: stalled streams rate dropped to ~0.02%, memory steady. On control pool stalled rate ~0.28% and memory rising.

anya: That's a pretty clear signal for flow-control/idle handling. Next: quantify perf impact of higher idle timeout (latency tail?).

tony: Action items:
- maria: monitor canary for 2h, collect pcap + metrics (done)
- kevin: post pcap to S3 and share link, grep for FIN/RST pattern
- anya: prepare PR to tune http2 window update thresholds and add guard for half-closed streams in upstream writer
- infra-oncall: hold off on conntrack changes until we have final root cause

maria: Will do. If canary stays stable we'll plan a staged rollout across us-west within 3 hours and a rollback plan.

kevin: pcap upload: s3://redwood-debug/1729004321-edge-h2c-canary.pcap (private).

sre-bot: INC-20241118-334 updated: canary looks healthy, priority remains P2.

maria: Thanks all. I'll post follow-ups after the 2h window. :thumbsup:
